metadata.title: KP02 · Basis, projection, and reconstruction
metadata.description: Reasoning-led 2.3.1; editable native teaching deck; global manual mode; no narration.

tools-title.name: tools-title
tools-title.text: Build a vector from directional contributions

tools-context.name: tools-context
tools-context.text: A vector contains ordered readings; a scalar scales it. An inner product sums entrywise products.

tools-source.name: tools-source
tools-source.text: PR · KP02 · 1/11  |  Handout §1,§2  |  Manual Next / Prev

tools-bubble.name: tools-bubble
tools-bubble.text: Follow the rightward and upward contributions from the origin, then verify their sum.

basis-title.name: basis-title
basis-title.text: Tilted directions can also measure observations

basis-context.name: basis-context
basis-context.text: A basis uniquely represents every vector. An orthonormal basis also has perpendicular unit directions.

basis-source.name: basis-source
basis-source.text: PR · KP02 · 2/11  |  Handout §2,§7  |  Manual Next / Prev

basis-bubble.name: basis-bubble
basis-bubble.text: Inspect the directions, then check their lengths and inner product.

dot-product-title.name: dot-product-title
dot-product-title.text: Measure a directional contribution with an inner product

dot-product-context.name: dot-product-context
dot-product-context.text: $y_j=\mathbf u_j^T\mathbf x$ is the signed contribution along unit direction $j$.

dot-product-source.name: dot-product-source
dot-product-source.text: PR · KP02 · 3/11  |  Handout §3  |  Manual Next / Prev

dot-product-bubble.name: dot-product-bubble
dot-product-bubble.text: Pair corresponding entries, multiply, then add the products.

coordinates-title.name: coordinates-title
coordinates-title.text: Collect both inner products as new coordinates

coordinates-context.name: coordinates-context
coordinates-context.text: Store basis directions in columns. Transpose $T$ makes rows that multiply the observation column.

coordinates-source.name: coordinates-source
coordinates-source.text: PR · KP02 · 4/11  |  Handout §3  |  Manual Next / Prev

coordinates-bubble.name: coordinates-bubble
coordinates-bubble.text: Match rows: each row inner product produces one score.

rebuild-title.name: rebuild-title
rebuild-title.text: Scale the directions back and add them

rebuild-context.name: rebuild-context
rebuild-context.text: Use the same input space and equal axis scales. Retain both scores, $y_1=10,y_2=5$.

rebuild-source.name: rebuild-source
rebuild-source.text: PR · KP02 · 5/11  |  Handout §4  |  Manual Next / Prev

rebuild-bubble.name: rebuild-bubble
rebuild-bubble.text: Follow the two head-to-tail contributions and check whether their endpoint recovers the observation.

truncate-title.name: truncate-title
truncate-title.text: Discarding a score removes its contribution

truncate-context.name: truncate-context
truncate-context.text: Retain only $y_1=10$. The observation $(2,11)$ and original basis stay unchanged.

truncate-source.name: truncate-source
truncate-source.text: PR · KP02 · 6/11  |  Handout §5  |  Manual Next / Prev

truncate-bubble.name: truncate-bubble
truncate-bubble.text: Follow the residual from the reconstruction to the original observation and measure its squared length.

image-basis-title.name: image-basis-title
image-basis-title.text: Images can be assembled from basis patterns

image-basis-context.name: image-basis-context
image-basis-context.text: Added: a two-by-two image has four pixels. Basis colors encode signs, not photographic brightness.

image-basis-source.name: image-basis-source
image-basis-source.text: PR · KP02 · 7/11  |  Handout §6  |  Manual Next / Prev

image-basis-bubble.name: image-basis-bubble
image-basis-bubble.text: Treat the pixel matrix as four readings; inspect the sign pattern of each basis image.

image-basis-definition.name: image-basis-definition
image-basis-definition.text: $F$ denotes the entrywise inner product; these four patterns are orthonormal.

image-coefficients-title.name: image-coefficients-title
image-coefficients-title.text: Compute every image coefficient from visible inputs

image-coefficients-context.name: image-coefficients-context
image-coefficients-context.text: Use the same image $X$. Each row supplies its basis and the four-product sum.

image-coefficients-source.name: image-coefficients-source
image-coefficients-source.text: PR · KP02 · 8/11  |  Handout §6  |  Manual Next / Prev

image-coefficients-bubble.name: image-coefficients-bubble
image-coefficients-bubble.text: Verify the signs in each row. What disappears if only the first pattern is retained?

image-reconstruction-title.name: image-reconstruction-title
image-reconstruction-title.text: What pixels remain with only the common pattern?

image-reconstruction-context.name: image-reconstruction-context
image-reconstruction-context.text: Retain coefficient five for the common pattern and zero the other scores. Keep original pixels and basis visible.

image-reconstruction-source.name: image-reconstruction-source
image-reconstruction-source.text: PR · KP02 · 9/11  |  Handout §6  |  Manual Next / Prev

image-reconstruction-bubble.name: image-reconstruction-bubble
image-reconstruction-bubble.text: Scale each basis pixel, subtract reconstruction from input, and verify all four residuals.

conditions-context.name: conditions-context
conditions-context.text: Orthonormal bases satisfy $U^TU=I$. General invertible bases require solving equations; complex data use a conjugate transpose.

conditions-source.name: conditions-source
conditions-source.text: PR · KP02 · 10/11  |  Handout §7,§8  |  Manual Next / Prev

conditions-bubble.name: conditions-bubble
conditions-bubble.text: Use the same observation to test what happens when nonorthogonal directions are treated as orthonormal.

conditions-naive.name: conditions-naive
conditions-naive.text: $\begin{gathered}(\mathbf b_1^T\mathbf x,\mathbf b_2^T\mathbf x)=(2,13)\\2\mathbf b_1+13\mathbf b_2=(15,13)^T\end{gathered}$

new-vector-title.name: new-vector-title
new-vector-title.text: Scores and discarded error for a new vector

new-vector-context.name: new-vector-context
new-vector-context.text: New vector $(9,2)^T$; use orthonormal directions $(3/5,4/5)^T$ and $(-4/5,3/5)^T$.

new-vector-source.name: new-vector-source
new-vector-source.text: PR · KP02 · 11/11  |  Handout §9,§10  |  Manual Next / Prev

new-vector-bubble.name: new-vector-bubble
new-vector-bubble.text: Compute both scores and first-direction squared error. State why direct inner products are valid.
